title: What Kind of Lover Are You?

chapters.title: How you fall
chapters.teaser: Fast, slow, sideways or all at once. The way your soul actually falls for someone.

chapters.title: Your flirting style
chapters.teaser: What you think you're doing, what they think you're doing, and the one move that lands.

chapters.title: Your attachment pattern
chapters.teaser: Clingy, cool, steady or somewhere in between. How you hold on when you care.

chapters.title: Jealousy and your trigger
chapters.teaser: The exact thing that sets you off, and what you do instead of saying it.

chapters.title: Yeon's red flag report
chapters.teaser: The love habit you keep repeating. Yeon does not soften this chapter.

chapters.title: What you actually need
chapters.teaser: Not your type. Your match. The kind of person and love that lets you relax.

text.how-you-fall: You fall fast and in public. Byeong is the sun, and the sun has never once been subtle. When you like someone, everyone knows by Friday, including your group chat, your mum and possibly the barista. You fall for energy: someone who laughs at your jokes, who matches your enthusiasm, who makes ordinary nights feel like an event. The first weeks with you are a highlight reel. Spontaneous plans, big gestures, you making them feel like the most interesting person in any room. The tricky part comes when the shine settles into routine. You love loving, and you can mistake a quiet phase for a dying flame. It usually isn't. Real warmth doesn't need to be at full brightness all the time. Even the sun has evenings.
text.flirting: Your flirting is generous and slightly overwhelming, in a fun way. You compliment loudly, you tease, you make the plan, you pay for the snacks, you invite them to the thing with your twelve friends. You flirt like you're hosting. People feel instantly welcome, which is why you're so easy to crush on. The flip side is that your warmth is the same for everyone, so the person you actually like may not realize they're special. They watched you light up the whole table. Here's the move: give them something you don't give the room. Quiet attention. Lower your voice, ask a real question, and stay on their answer for longer than feels natural. Your spotlight is lovely. Your undivided focus is unforgettable.
text.attachment: You look secure, and a lot of the time you are. You're optimistic about love, you forgive quickly, you don't hold grudges, you assume the best. Underneath, there's a quieter need: you want to be seen shining. If a partner stops reacting, stops noticing, stops laughing, you don't get anxious exactly, you get bored and a little hurt, and you might go looking for an audience elsewhere. Not cheating, just more attention from friends, more plans, more noise. Your growth edge is staying through the dull middle. Love includes Tuesdays where nothing happens and nobody applauds. If you can feel warm on those days too, without needing a reaction, you become the kind of partner people build whole lives around.
text.jealousy: You don't expect to be jealous, so when it hits it surprises you. Your trigger is attention. If your person is lit up by someone else, laughing harder at their jokes, more animated in their conversation, you feel it like a cloud crossing your face. You might not say anything. Instead, you turn the brightness up. Louder stories, bigger plans, more charm aimed in their direction. It works, sometimes, but it's exhausting and a bit transparent. Try naming it with a smile instead: "Okay, I'm a tiny bit jealous of how much you like her jokes." Said lightly, this is disarming and honest. People love you for your openness. Being open about the not-so-sunny feelings is the same skill, just pointed inward.
text.red-flag: Yeon's verdict: you make promises at full brightness and keep them at half. "We should go to Jeju together!" "I'll cook you dinner every Sunday!" You mean every word in the moment. Then life happens, and the person who believed you is quietly disappointed. Second flag: you hate heavy talks. When things get serious, you crack a joke, change the subject, or suggest getting food. It feels like keeping things light. To your partner it can feel like you're never fully there for the hard stuff. Third: you need an audience, and a partner can start to feel like one. Love is not a show with a crowd. Make fewer promises, keep more of them, and let someone see you when you're not performing.
text.what-you-need: You need appreciation, sincerely and often. Not empty flattery, which you see through, but someone who notices what you do and tells you. "That was so thoughtful." "You made that party." You need a partner with their own glow, too: someone with passions and plans so you don't feel responsible for keeping the whole relationship lit. You do well with people who are calm without being cold, who can be your steady evening when your day has been loud. And you need room to be social. A partner who resents your friends or your plans will dim you fast. The ideal person for you laughs easily, says what they feel, and still loves you on the days you are cloudy and quiet.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Byeong, you love like sunshine. Big, warm, generous. Everyone feels invited.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Exactly. Everyone. Including the person you're not dating. They're confused.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You're just naturally warm! Your first dates are legendary.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Your first dates, yes. Your fourth month when it gets quiet and you get restless? Less legendary.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Give your person the attention you don't give the room. That's the real gift.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Fewer promises about Jeju. More actually showing up on Tuesday.

spring.intro: Spring is Wood's season, and Wood feeds Fire, so a spring-born Byeong Fire is the rising sun with a full tank. You fall quickly and optimistically, convinced every new crush might be the big one, and your enthusiasm is honestly contagious. You love courting: the plans, the surprises, the long walks that turn into long talks. With so much fuel behind you, the risk is that you burn through the beginning and then wonder why the middle feels flat. Your love grows when you aim the light instead of spraying it. Choose one person, one plan, one honest conversation. Earth, the element your Fire feeds, is your lesson: turn a spark into something people can stand on.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Spring Byeong, you said 'soulmate' after brunch. Let it be a Tuesday before it's destiny.

summer.intro: Summer is Fire's own season, so a summer-born Byeong is the noon sun: blazing, generous and slightly too much. Everyone feels your warmth, and that is the issue in love. Your partner may adore your brightness and still feel like one of many people basking in it. You crave reaction. When affection goes quiet, you turn up the volume with bigger gestures, louder jokes, a busier calendar. Doubled Fire needs Water and Earth for balance, which in a relationship means listening without performing and showing up in plain ways. The most romantic thing you can do is sit still, phone face down, and let them be the interesting one for an evening.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Summer Byeong, they don't need fireworks nightly. They need you, at normal brightness, staying.

autumn.intro: In autumn Metal rules, and Fire controls Metal. A sun setting over a harvest field works hard for what it gets, so an autumn-born Byeong Fire loves through effort. You are the partner who fixes things, organises the trip, brings home the good bread. You treat love as something you earn, and you are generous with the earnings. Spending your heat on outcomes can leave you tired and quietly resentful when the effort is not matched. Wood, your fuel element, is what refills you: inspiration, encouragement, someone who believes in you before you have done anything impressive. Let yourself be loved for showing up, not just for what you produce.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Autumn Byeong, you don't have to fix their week to be loved this week. Just sit down.

winter.intro: Winter belongs to Water, and Water puts out Fire. A winter-born Byeong is the low December sun: rare, precious, and working to be felt. You might be the warmest person in your friend group and still feel unsure whether your love is welcome. That makes you try hard in romance. You overextend early, then retreat when you sense the slightest chill. People treasure your warmth precisely because the season is cold, so you are often more loved than you think. Wood feeds you, and in love that means a partner who encourages you, plans with you and says 'I'm glad you're here.' Pick someone who adds kindling, not someone who tests your flame.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Winter Byeong, a little sun in December means more than a whole July. You're that sun.

strength.strong: A strong Byeong Fire is a sun with nothing to block it. Your chart has plenty of Fire and Wood, which makes you magnetic, generous and very used to being the centre. In love that looks like big feelings, big plans and a partner who sometimes feels like your audience. Your blind spot is overpowering: filling every silence, taking over conversations, expecting their enthusiasm to match yours instantly. Turn the brightness toward them. Ask a question and then wait through the pause. Let them pick the plan, tell the story, hold the spotlight. Your warmth lands deeper when it is aimed rather than broadcast.
strength.weak: A weak Byeong Fire is the sun behind clouds, still warm but working hard to be felt. With little Fire or Wood in your chart, you give affection generously and then wonder whether it was enough. You may over-perform cheerfulness, cover your own bad days, and keep relationships alive with gestures you cannot really afford to make. Your blind spot is over-giving to stay lovable. Rest without explaining yourself. Let someone else plan the surprise for once. Notice which people still warm toward you when you are tired and quiet. Those are the ones worth your light.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood in your chart turns love into a growth plan. You want things to move forward, define the relationship, make progress, and slow phases make you restless. You can also be stubborn in arguments, holding your position like a tree in wind. In love this looks like big intentions and a little impatience. Balance it with Metal energy: clear agreements, pruning what isn't working, and accepting that some things are already finished growing. Not every relationship needs to become a forest. Some are perfect as a single, steady tree.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means beginnings are your hard part. You might wait for the other person to make the first move, define things, or suggest the next step, and you can stay in a comfortable but stuck situation for too long. Your love is real, it just doesn't push. Balance it by practising small starts: suggest the date, send the first text, say what you hope for out loud. Green things help as reminders, a plant by your bed, a green phone case. Love grows when someone plants it. Sometimes that someone is you.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire makes your love bright, fast and a little combustible. You fall hard, flirt boldly and feel everything at full volume. The highs are glorious. The lows, when attention drops, feel like the lights went out. You can also lose interest once the excitement settles. Balance it with Water energy: slowing down, letting quiet evenings count, and sitting with feelings before reacting. Ask yourself if you love the person or the thrill. The best flame for you burns steady, not just bright.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means passion and visibility don't come easily in love. You might care deeply but struggle to show it, hold back affection until you're sure, or feel awkward with romantic gestures. People can mistake your reserve for disinterest. Balance it by letting warmth out in small, brave doses: a compliment, a hug that lasts a second longer, a little playfulness. Warm colours and sunlight help you feel more expressive. You don't need fireworks. You just need people to see that the light is on.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth makes you a steady, devoted partner who can get a little stuck. You value security, routine and loyalty, and you might stay in familiar patterns even when they've stopped making you happy. Change feels risky. You may also over-care, taking on your partner's problems as your own. Balance it with Wood energy: try something new together, plan an adventure, let the relationship grow in surprising directions. Safe is wonderful. Safe and alive is even better.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth means love can feel unsteady. You might worry about where things stand, struggle to settle into commitment, or jump between highs and lows. You can also find it hard to trust that someone will stay. Balance it by building small, reliable rituals: a weekly date, a regular call, a shared routine. Choose partners who are consistent rather than exciting. Earth tones and home-cooked meals help you feel grounded. Stability isn't boring. For you, it's what lets love feel safe enough to enjoy.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal gives you strong standards and very clear boundaries in love. You know what you want and what you won't tolerate, which is healthy, until it becomes rigid. You can be critical, quick to judge, or end things abruptly when disappointed. Balance it with Fire energy: warmth, forgiveness, play. Let small mistakes be small. Say the kind thing before the honest thing. Strong boundaries keep you safe. Soft edges let people actually come close enough to love you.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal means boundaries are your hard part in love. You might say yes when you mean no, stay too long, or let people treat you less well than you deserve because you don't want conflict. Your heart is open, sometimes too open. Balance it by practising clear, simple limits: "I'm not okay with that," without a long explanation. Decluttering and white or silver accents can help you feel sharper. Boundaries aren't walls. They're the frame that makes the picture of your love clear.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water makes your love deep, intuitive and sometimes overwhelming. You feel everything, read every mood and can get lost in emotional currents or imagined stories. You may also avoid commitment, drifting rather than choosing. Balance it with Earth energy: grounding conversations, practical plans, partners who are steady and clear. Write down what actually happened before reacting to what you feel happened. Your depth is beautiful. It just needs a shore so you don't get swept away.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means emotional depth and rest don't come easily in love. You might stay busy, keep conversations practical, or struggle to sit with vulnerable feelings, yours or your partner's. Love can feel like a to-do list. Balance it with slow, quiet moments: late talks, journaling, listening without fixing. Navy and black, water by your bed, and slow evenings help you soften. You don't need to drown in feelings. Just let yourself wade in a little deeper.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood: you want it defined, labelled and growing by Thursday. Breathe.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: Your hope is beautiful. Let it grow at the speed of a real person.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: you fall hard, fast and loudly. Then the second act bores you.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion is a gift. Let it simmer a while. Slow love tastes better.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Too much Earth: staying somewhere stale because leaving takes effort isn't loyalty. It's inertia.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your loyalty is rare. Make sure it's going somewhere that still feeds you.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Too much Metal: your dating checklist has forty points. Nobody passes. Including you.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Standards protect you. Leave one door open for someone surprising.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Too much Water: you wrote a whole love story in your head. They've read none of it.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your depth is gorgeous. Share a little of it with the real person.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood? Love won't start itself. Send the first text. Plant something.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: Waiting for them to make the move isn't patience. It's hiding behind a nice word.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire? Your love is real, it just whispers. Let someone hear it.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: A compliment you only think doesn't count. Say it, then survive the blushing.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth? You love brightly but drift. A small weekly ritual keeps you anchored.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: Three crushes, zero follow-through. Pick one and show up twice in a row.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal? Your kindness needs a boundary. A no keeps your yes worth something.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: Three cancellations and a fourth chance isn't generosity. It's a pattern you're funding.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water? You act before you feel. Pause and ask what you actually want.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: Over someone in a weekend isn't healing. It's skipping the chapter. Read it.
